commandConfig.description: A hook or alias command in one of three TOML forms. A string is a single command (`pre-start = "npm ci"`). A table runs named commands concurrently (`[post-start]` with `server = "npm run dev"`). A pipeline array runs steps in sequence (`pre-start = ["npm ci", { build = "npm run build" }]`), equivalently written as repeated `[[hook]]` blocks. Within a step, multiple keys run concurrently; a failing step aborts the rest of the pipeline. Names cannot contain colons. Values are minijinja templates (see https://worktrunk.dev/hook/#template-variables); `pre-*` hooks block on failure while `post-*` hooks run in the background. Project commands prompt for approval on first run.

oneOf.description: Named commands running concurrently, e.g. `[post-start]` with `server = "npm run dev"`. One key is a single named step; multiple keys run together.

propertyNames.description: Hook command names cannot contain colons (breaks log-spec parsing).

oneOf.description: Pipeline: steps run in sequence. Each entry is a command string (anonymous step) or a named table (one key serial, several keys concurrent). Equivalently written as repeated `[[hook]]` blocks.
Named pipeline step: one key runs serially, several keys run concurrently.

commandConfig.title: CommandConfig

description:
Project configuration for Worktrunk, stored at `.config/wt.toml` and checked into git. Shared team settings: lifecycle hooks, dev-server URL, forge, commit-message append fragment, copy-ignored excludes, and project aliases.

Source: https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/tree/main (src/config/project.rs, src/config/hooks.rs, src/config/commands.rs). Docs: https://worktrunk.dev/config/ (project configuration), https://worktrunk.dev/hook/ (hook types, forms, template variables). Starter file: `wt config create --project`.

aliases.description: Command templates that run as `wt <name>`, shared with teammates. Each value takes the same three hook forms. All hook template variables are available (e.g. `{{ branch }}`, `{{ worktree_path }}`). For personal aliases use the user config `[aliases]` section instead. See https://worktrunk.dev/extending/#aliases.

ci.description: Deprecated: use `[forge]` instead. `wt config update` moves `platform` to `[forge]`. Aliased at runtime — `[forge].platform` takes precedence where both are set.

platform.description: Deprecated alias for `[forge].platform`. Same accepted values.

commit.description: Project-wide commit-message settings shared across teammates. Only `generation.template-append` is honored from the project file; the LLM command and the main prompt template stay in user config.

generation.description: Commit-message generation settings shared across the team.

template-append.description: Text appended to the commit and squash prompts inside a `<project-guidance>` block. Rendered with the same minijinja context as the main template (`{{ branch }}`, `{{ git_diff }}`, …). The first time the fragment is used (and whenever it changes), `wt` prompts the user to approve it — the same one-shot gate as project-defined hooks.

forge.description: Names the forge explicitly, for a remote whose hostname carries no forge name for detection to read (a Forgejo instance at `forge.example.com`, a company git server). Detection otherwise reads `github`, `gitlab`, or `gitea` anywhere in the host, plus the Azure DevOps service domains. A repository's own `[forge]` wins over user-config `[projects]` entries, field by field.

hostname.description: API hostname for GitHub Enterprise or self-hosted GitLab. Only needed when the remote URL uses an SSH host alias that does not resolve to the real API hostname.

platform.description: Forge platform. Picks the forge CLI (`gh`, `glab`, `tea`, or `az`) for the `wt switch pr:` shortcut and `wt list --full` CI status. When unset, the platform is detected from the remote URL.

list.description: Project-level settings for `wt list` output. Only `url` belongs here; list display defaults (full, branches, columns, …) are user config.

url.description: URL template for dev-server links shown in `wt list`. Example: "http://localhost:{{ branch | hash_port }}". Available filters: `sanitize`, `hash_port`. Shown dimmed when the port is not listening.

post-commit.description: CI triggers, notifications, background linting. Runs after committing. Background.

post-create.description: Deprecated alias for `post-start`. Both names load, but `wt config update` renames this to `post-start`. Prefer `post-start` in new config.

post-merge.description: Deployment, notifications, installing updated binaries. Runs in the target branch worktree if it exists, otherwise the primary worktree. Background.

post-remove.description: Stopping dev servers, removing containers, notifying external systems. The active worktree is gone, so it runs in the primary worktree; template variables still reference the removed worktree. Background.

post-start.description: Runs once when a new worktree is created, in the background. Use for dev servers, long builds, file watchers, and `wt step copy-ignored`. Prefer over `pre-start` unless a later step needs the work completed first.

post-switch.description: Triggers on all switch results: creating, switching to existing, or staying on current. Background; output goes to hook logs (`wt config state logs`).

pre-commit.description: Formatters, linters, type checking. Runs before any Worktrunk commit (`wt step commit`, `wt step squash`, and the commit `wt merge` makes). Blocking and fail-fast. During `wt merge` the blocking hooks run pre-commit → pre-merge → pre-remove.

pre-create.description: Deprecated alias for `pre-start`. Both names load, but `wt config update` renames this to `pre-start`. Prefer `pre-start` in new config.

pre-merge.description: Tests, security scans, build verification. Runs after rebase, before merge to target. Blocking and fail-fast.

pre-remove.description: Cleanup before worktree deletion: saving test artifacts, backing up state. Runs in the worktree being removed. Blocking and fail-fast.

pre-start.description: Runs once when a new worktree is created, blocking `post-start`/`--execute` until complete. Use for dependency install and env-file generation. Blocking and fail-fast.

pre-switch.description: Runs in the source worktree before switching — creating, switching to existing, or staying on current. Blocking and fail-fast: failure aborts the switch.

copy-ignored.description: Additional excludes for `wt step copy-ignored`. Built-in excludes (VCS metadata and tool-state directories) always apply; user-config and project-config exclusions are combined.
